proposal.hypothesis: The earlier scalar unroll schedules were correct but slower than the 55.00 µs baseline (the best recorded was four groups at 63.81 µs). This contrasting two-group schedule interleaves independent table lookups, then validates and commits the first group before deciding whether to commit the second. It tests whether that lookup overlap and reduced loop control can help without the larger live set or delayed combined validation; no speedup is assumed.

retained: Unrolled the existing scalar decoder to load and interleave table lookups for two independent eight-character blocks per bulk iteration.
Validated and stored the first block before validating and storing the second; if the second block is invalid, execution resumes in the unchanged bytewise decoder at that block.
Used a 19-character guard to leave the existing scalar tail/padding path intact and retain safe input/output bounds.
Added no explicit SIMD, parallel execution, benchmark-size specialization, or changes outside src/candidate.cpp.

proposal.hypothesis: Earlier scalar schedules were correct but slower than the 55.00 µs baseline: two groups measured 82.32 µs, three groups 147.64 µs, four groups 63.81 µs, and eight groups 81.30 µs. This experiment uses four independent groups with table lookups interleaved across groups, then validates and commits each group in order instead of delaying a combined validity decision. Interleaving may expose independent lookup work while per-group checks constrain live values and preserve fallback behavior; the larger schedule can still lose to register pressure or code size. No speedup is assumed.

retained: Replaced the two-group bulk loop with a four-group, 32-character scalar loop guarded by 37 remaining characters to leave tail/padding work to the existing scalar decoder.
Loaded and table-decoded four independent eight-character blocks, interleaving the eight lookup positions across blocks to expose independent scalar lookup chains.
Validated and wrote each decoded block in input order, advancing pointers only after that block passes validation; retained existing bytewise fallback for invalid data, padding, and tails.
Added no explicit SIMD, parallel execution, benchmark-length specialization, or changes outside src/candidate.cpp.
